To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the inertial and droo controls are essential for the wind turbine to participate in frequency support.
the inertial control and the droop control are essential for the wind turbine for providing frequency support.
the frequency support by using wind turbine with inertial control is more effective than without control.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the frequency regulation by using wind turbine with inertial control, droop control and varying the droop parameter.
frequency response analysis of DFIG based WTGs with inertial and droops control techniques.
investigating the impact of increasing level of wind power on the frequency response of the power system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the wind power plants equipped with inertial and droops controllers are capable of providing frequency support to the power grid.
the frequency response of grid with wind power is improved by increasing the wind power potential with inertial control as well as droop control.
the wind turbines can provide the short term frequency regulation to the grid with the help of both inertial control and frequency droop control.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the wind power plant with frequency regulation techniques would be able to provide frequency support in the event of large disturbances.
, the frequency regulation techniques have significant impact on frequency response of the system.
the inertial control is not capable to provide frequency support for higher installed wind power capacity and the droop controller can be used to provide frequency support in such condition.
The main takeaway from our work is that
wind turbine can participate in frequency control and can provide significant frequency support to the power system.
, wind power plants can be utilized as frequency support in power system.
the frequency response of the system improves with increasing wind power potential when operated with frequency regulation techniques.
